name: Casa Kakmo
notes: Refined 13 Oct 2026 (second pass, court re-laid): the court is now a narrow ~7 m passage running the lot's depth, as in photos 00-04: the main house (glazed ground floor, yellow upper with three tall slits, grey concrete bands) along the west side, a tall yellow wall with a small horizontal window along the east, the pool 4 m wide and 16.6 m long between them with a ledge and entry step, the stair of floating treads rising along the main house to the guest block's roof, the guest block closing the north end (ribbon window, slit, palms in pots, sunbeds), its roof lounge under the canopy; the street wall at the south. The east wall and party walls were lowered to 4-5 m so the pool and stair show from above (the photographs' walls are taller, about 6 m). Positions of all of it within the lot are guessed. Earlier pass: the pool now fills the court between the two houses from the guest block's face to the glazed ground floor (it had stopped 3.6 m long), with a pale ledge and shallow white entry step along the guest block as in photos 00-02; the paved apron moved to the east end beside the palms; a rear tree trimmed. Still guessed: the real court is narrower and longer than drawn (the pool in the photographs runs the lot's depth), and the lot's orientation. From the pool-court views (00-04, 06): the pool runs across the lot between the two houses, the main house's glazed ground floor on one long side and the yellow guest block's long face (one horizontal window, one slit) on the other, a pale ledge along the yellow wall and a paved strip along the glass; a floating stair of cantilevered treads on the white west end wall climbing to the guest block's roof; palms in pots and sunbeds on gravel beside the guest block at the pool's east end, a timber screen behind; on the guest roof a sunken U of yellow benches with white cushions and grasses behind, under a concrete canopy on a steel frame that runs out east over the palms; the main house's upper storey yellow with three tall narrow windows between a grey concrete band and a grey parapet. This pass: Izamal yellow drawn as yellow (was ochre); the pool widened to fill the court and ended at the guest block's east corner as the photographs show; the stair re-stepped to reach the guest roof at its face; the roof lounge given its yellow U bench, cushions, table and grasses; the palms drawn as palms in dark pots; the main house's parapet band deepened and its roof drawn pale; the party walls kept only round the court (the main house fills the lot's width). Orientation guessed: street to the south, rear garden to the north. The street front, the rear garden, the ends of the main house and the lot's exact dimensions were not shown and are guessed from a typical narrow Yucatecan lot; the pool's entry steps and the stair's railing are too fine to draw. Refined 24 Sep 2026: the garden trees behind the guest block made smaller and pushed to the rear corners, so the roof lounge and the yellow block read (they swamped it); broad pale entry steps at the pool's east end; the stair's dark steel railing; the main house's outer walls pale render rather than grey concrete (only the band over the glass is concrete, as photographed); the street front, which no photograph shows, painted Izamal yellow with a white plinth and cornice, a timber door and two windows - a guess following the town's rule that its facades are yellow. Stair railing omitted in the second pass (the posts read as heavy bars).
